content.text: All responsive provisions inspected (24.1–24.4, plus 13.3 licence transfer and 9.2 insolvency). No redline needed.

input.quote: 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates.
input.rationale: Section 24 meets our preferred position in full. 24.1 gives Customer a consent-free right to assign to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all assets (prompt notice only, which is not a consent condition). 24.2 bars Vendor assignment, delegation of material performance, or transfer by change of control without our prior written consent, with the reasonableness standard running in our favour, and bars assignment to a direct Customer competitor. 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any termination, suspension, repricing, acceleration or service-reduction right on our change of control, so we are clear of walk-away territory. 24.3's residual mutual consent requirement applies only to "other assignments" and therefore does not cut back the 24.1 carve-out, and 13.3 aligns by letting Customer transfer licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with a Section 24-permitted assignment. Only minor point short of ideal wording: 24.2's competitor bar is expressed as "without Customer's consent" rather than absolute, but that leaves the discretion with us and is noted rather than redlined.
